top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct architecture, not a refinement of the 2005 comb or 2012 single-ion prizes. It cancels the light shift while keeping Lamb-Dicke confinement of many atoms. Performance near 1e-18 is confirmed across laboratories and species. The two-name credit (Katori for the concept and first strontium clock, Ye for the accuracy frontier) is separable and uncontested, and a citation worded around the lattice concept keeps clear of earlier prizes. This is a mature, well-attributed achievement, clearly preferable to no award.
